title: Effects of 4-nonylphenol on oxidant/antioxidant balance system inducing hepatic steatosis in male rat.
ehr_evidence: The study used 24 male Sprague-Dawley rats (70–80 g) from the Experimental Animal Center of Tongji Medical College; data were derived from intraperitoneal 4-nonylphenol administration, serum hepatic marker enzyme assays, liver histology, TUNEL/PCNA immunohistochemistry, and liver gene expression profiling (RT-PCR) — no electronic or computerised individual-level health records were used.
summary: In a controlled subchronic animal toxicology study, intraperitoneal administration of 4-nonylphenol (0, 2, 10, 50 mg/kg) to male Sprague-Dawley rats for 30 days induced hepatic steatosis associated with oxidative stress, decreased antioxidants, and apoptosis.
key_findings: Serum GOT, GPT and LDH were significantly increased in 4-NP-treated groups versus control (p < 0.01, p < 0.001) and γ-GT was significantly increased (p < 0.05).
H2O2 levels were significantly increased at 50 mg/kg (p < 0.01) and MDA levels significantly increased at 10 and 50 mg/kg (p < 0.01).
Antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, CAT, GSH-Px) were significantly decreased in 4-NP-treated groups versus control (p < 0.05, p < 0.01, p < 0.001).
Liver SOD1 and GPx expression significantly decreased (p < 0.05, p < 0.01) while HSP70 expression significantly increased (p < 0.05).
Caspase-9 and Bax expression significantly increased (p < 0.05) while Bcl-2 expression significantly decreased (p < 0.05).
Fas, FasL and TNF-α expression significantly increased (p < 0.05, p < 0.01).
TUNEL-positive apoptotic cells significantly increased at 10 and 50 mg/kg versus none in controls.
PCNA-positive cell index was 4.64%, 8.87% and 9.07% at 2, 10 and 50 mg/kg respectively versus negligible in controls.
Relative liver weight was significantly increased at 10 and 50 mg/kg (p < 0.05) with no significant change in final body weight.
captured_features: Serum GOT, GPT, LDH, γ-GT activities
Liver gene expression (SOD1, GPx, HSP70, Caspase-9, Bax, Bcl-2, Fas, FasL, TNF-α) via RT-PCR
Liver histology grades (steatosis, ballooning, lobular inflammation)
Body weight, absolute and relative liver weight
study_design: Controlled experimental subchronic exposure (animal toxicology) study
population: 24 male Sprague-Dawley rats, 70–80 g, from Tongji Medical College Animal Laboratory, Wuhan, China
limitations: Only male rats used, limiting sex-generalizability
Acute/subchronic intraperitoneal exposure may not reflect real-world human exposure routes
Rat model may not translate to humans
